races.title: State House, District 9
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Timothy Reeder
cands.bio: Emergency physician and educator from Ayden, Pitt County. Taught at East Carolina University's Brody School of Medicine, served as Chief of Medical Staff at Vidant Medical Center, and was 2019 president of the North Carolina Medical Society. Republican member of the NC House for District 9 since January 2023.
cands.gaps: We could not read his full sponsored-bill list or any record of what he did on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, or gun policy. We found no stated positions from him on those topics. His raised-as-a-child location is not stated; only a Catholic education through high school is mentioned. We found no notable endorsements (Ballotpedia lists none for 2022, 2024 or 2026) and no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages available. His campaign site lists themes such as affordability, healthcare and protecting taxpayer dollars, but gives no specifics. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys.

local.label: Roots 55: Born in Columbus, Ohio, he moved to North Carolina as an adult in 1998 (about 28 years ago) and now lives in Ayden.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Physician (M.D., Ohio State 1995; MPH, UNC-Chapel Hill) who taught at ECU's Brody School of Medicine and held leadership roles at Vidant/ECU Health, including Chief of Medical Staff. He has served in the NC House since 2023.
qual.why: He has real prior legislative service (elected 2022, re-elected 2024) plus a professional career with management and health-policy experience. Board and society roles were not counted.
qual.label: He has real prior legislative service (elected 2022, re-elected 2024) plus a professional career with management and health-policy experience. Board and society roles were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he supports charter schools and parental choice in education, and that teacher salaries must be competitive and reward the best performers.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he listed support for police and firefighters among his beliefs.

pro-life.evidence: Wikipedia reports he campaigned on opposing abortion and believes abortion should be legally limited to the first twelve weeks of pregnancy in most cases. This is a restriction position, not a no-exceptions one.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: Born in Columbus, Ohio, he moved to North Carolina as an adult in 1998 (about 28 years ago) and now lives in Ayden.

cands.name: Claire Kempner
cands.bio: Pitt County mother of three and community advocate. Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 9 in 2024 and 2026, losing to Republican incumbent Timothy Reeder in 2024. Has volunteered with local schools and community organizations.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations for 2026 from Sway voting groups, including Before the Day, Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Fair Map Fight Club and YALLvote. These are voter-guide groups, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Claire Kempner was born or raised. We found no record of her jobs or any office she has held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no documented positions from her on data centers, development, homestead taxes, land ownership, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice. Her campaign site is general, mentioning lower costs, public schools, fair maps, affordable healthcare and safe communities. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable organizational endorsements.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she moved to Pitt County in 2016, about ten years ago as an adult; her birthplace and upbringing are not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No job history is documented in the pages available. She describes herself as a mom and community advocate who volunteers with local schools and community organizations, and she has run for the state House twice without winning.
qual.why: No career or office held could be verified, so no score is given.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she will protect public schools and fight for strong public schools. It does not mention vouchers, charters or teacher pay, so this is only a loose fit with the plank.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she moved to Pitt County in 2016, about ten years ago as an adult; her birthplace and upbringing are not given.
